analysis:
Examined base text of the DistributedAutomaticBatchPlannerTests.swift test file (lines 1-778). The PR changes test lines around 772-834 on the head side. The visible patch excerpt shows that discoveryMode gains a `declared` parameter. Under `auto`, a coordinator-served cluster now asks for the Qwen speculative (MTP) assistant when the build declares the assistant public for the artifact. Explicit `on` and `off` behave as before. This is test-only code with constructed fixtures; it adds no runtime attack surface itself.

The production change it exercises is not supplied. That change is ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection.discoveryMode and the declaration source, likely ClusterPublicModels, which the fixture comment at line 47 references. Integration should verify three things:
(1) The `declared` flag derives from build-embedded, signed data, not operator-editable config or environment. Otherwise an operator (ADV-001) could enable the assistant on coordinator-served setups. That matters to T-054/T-056 and to the exactness of code and qualification identity (A-017).
(2) Coordinator-served setups carrying an assistant still match the coordinator's capability/configuration digests and qualification.
(3) automaticCandidate still verifies the inline artifact's manifest and aggregate digest. Base lines 760-761 show foreign IDs and digests throw.

The truncated patch (patch_excerpt_complete=false) hides head lines 785-834. Those may include additional negative controls, such as `off` with declared. No regression is identified from the test alone. The remaining test content concerns placement memory gates, link-probe history files (0600 permissions), served-speed build filtering, and the profile helper script. These lines are unchanged and are not security-relevant to this PR.
